name: update-grub
description: Debian/Ubuntu wrapper that regenerates the GRUB boot menu configuration from /etc/default/grub and detected kernels.

examples.explanation: The workflow: edit GRUB settings (timeout, default entry, kernel parameters via GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX), then regenerate.

examples.output:
Found linux image: /boot/vmlinuz-6.8.0-45-generic
Found linux image: /boot/vmlinuz-6.5.0-14-generic
examples.explanation: Confirms which kernels the boot menu will offer.

about: grub.cfg is generated — never edit it directly; edits vanish on the next update. The source of truth is /etc/default/grub (settings) and /etc/grub.d/ (scripts). On RHEL-family the equivalent is grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg.
useCases: Change boot timeout or default kernel.
Refresh the menu after installing a custom kernel.
mistakes: Forgetting to run update-grub after editing /etc/default/grub.
warnings: A broken GRUB update can make the system unbootable — keep a Live USB handy and verify the output lists your kernel.
distroNotes: Debian/Ubuntu-family convenience script. Other distros call grub2-mkconfig or grub-mkconfig directly.
